I am reconsidering whether to help p2 survive. If p1 captures both yellows and browns, the game is effectively over for everyone. p2's yellow set is complete with zero houses, while his brown houses are fully built.

I should buy one yellow property from p2 to break his monopoly. If p2 goes bankrupt to p1, p1 cannot complete the yellow set. That is a major defensive win.

I should offer cash for one yellow property from p2 to break his monopoly. Indiana is the cheapest option at face value.

I can afford to spend up to $237 on this trade. After subtracting that amount from my $852 cash and adding back the $185 mortgage cushion, I still need to survive an $800 orange rent.

I should keep a buffer so one orange rent does not force me to mortgage everything.

I now see that p1 owns St. Charles and States, but Virginia is unowned. I own Kentucky and p2 owns Indiana, so neither of us can complete the red monopoly.

A bankrupt player receives all of p2's properties, so p1 would inherit the full yellow and brown monopolies plus Indiana and Reading. Any single yellow purchase works to sever the monopoly, though Marvin is the most expensive and dangerous option.

I cannot afford to give him enough cash to survive the next orange rent, so he may only trade if he thinks a partial deal is better than total loss.
